subject: Performance SLO qualification & customer-led load test (FinWise)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@finwise.com>, Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO qualification & customer-led load test (FinWise)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Ben and Ellen — good to meet the FinWise team. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we can get your customer-led load test scheduled and scoped.

High-level SLOs and test targets (as discussed):
- Latency targets (typical prompt ~256 tokens, generation to first token + full gen):
  - p95 <= 200 ms
  - p99 <= 500 ms
- Throughput & concurrency:
  - Expected steady-state throughput target: 120 requests/sec (aggregate)
  - Expected peak concurrency: ~200 concurrent sessions (short bursts to 300)
- Streaming requirements:
  - Responses must support chunked streaming (server-sent/chunked) with tokens appearing as they generate. We should validate per-token latency and first-byte latency under load.
- Test profile:
  - 15m warmup, 30m steady-state, 10m cool-down; 3 variation runs (baseline / with KV cache / with batching)

Customer-led load test coordination (what we need from FinWise):
1) Test accounts: one or two test API keys scoped to a sandbox project (please provide key name(s) and a CSV of account IDs).
2) IP allowlist: public egress IPs for your runner(s) so we can ensure the call backs / webhooks (if any) are accepted. We can also provide our egress IP CIDRs for allowlisting.
3) Test window options: we suggested Wed 17 Mar 2027 09:00–12:00 PT (3h window) — please confirm preferred window and earliest blackout windows.
4) Test scripts: attached a k6 script (k6-finwise-v1.js) and a Locust file (locustfile_finwise.py) as starting points. Please review and let us know if you want modifications to the ramp profile, concurrency targets, or input prompts.

Attachments: k6-finwise-v1.js (javascript, 8KB) — k6 scenario with ramping/concurrency; locustfile_finwise.py (python, 6KB) — per-user streaming behavior stub.

Next steps / owners:
- Ben: please share test API key(s), test_account CSV, and confirm window (FinWise)
- FinWise Load Test Team: review scripts in the Drive link and flag any changes
- Rishi / Marissa: we'll prepare a sandbox route with monitoring dashboards, request tracing, and a temporary higher logging level for the window

If it helps, I pasted the target parameters into the Drive folder listed below so your load team can pick them up.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

--
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — that recap is perfect. A few quick clarifications / items from our side: 

- We can provide two test API keys (one per region) and a CSV of test_account_id, team, and test_priority. I attached test_accounts_finwise.csv.
- Window: Wed 17 Mar 2027 09:00–12:00 PT works for our load team — please consider this confirmed unless Redwood requests a different slot.
- Streaming: we do need per-token streaming validation. Our UI streams tokens to the user as they arrive, so first-byte latency under contention is the most important metric for us.
- Load runners: we will run k6 from our control plane (AWS eu-west-1) and a Locust cluster in us-west-2. We'll provide the public egress IPs before EOD Monday.

Attached: test_accounts_finwise.csv (1KB)
